exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
executionSteps: Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and turn your toes out slightly.
Take a breath, brace your stomach, and bend at the knees and hips together.
Lower until your thighs are roughly parallel to the floor, or as far as you can go without your lower back rounding.
Push the floor away and stand up, finishing with your hips fully extended.
commonMistakes: Letting the heels lift off the floor as you descend.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom instead of stopping at your usable depth.
Letting the knees collapse inward on the way up.
coachingCues: Spread the floor with your feet.
Chest stays proud all the way down.
Knees track over the middle of each foot.
safetyNotes: Reduce depth if you feel pinching at the front of the hip or sharp pain in the knee.
Hold a doorframe or bench for balance while you are learning the pattern.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
executionSteps: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest with both hands.
Stand with your feet about shoulder width apart and brace your stomach.
Squat between your knees, keeping your elbows inside your thighs.
Stand back up, keeping the weight pressed against your chest throughout.
commonMistakes: Letting the weight drift away from the chest, which pulls you forward.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears while holding the weight.
Bouncing out of the bottom instead of controlling the turnaround.
coachingCues: Hug the weight tight to the chest.
Elbows brush the inside of the knees.
safetyNotes: Start with a light weight, because the front-loaded position tires the upper back quickly.
Set the weight down rather than dropping it if your grip starts to fail.

exercises.name: Front Squat
executionSteps: Rack the bar across the front of your shoulders and lift your elbows until your upper arms are close to parallel with the floor.
Set your feet about shoulder width apart, brace, and descend by bending the knees.
Keep the torso as upright as you can and lower to the depth you can hold without the elbows dropping.
Drive up through your whole foot and keep the elbows high until the rep is finished.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows drop, which pulls the bar forward and rounds the upper back.
Leaning forward as if performing a back squat.
Gripping so tightly that the wrists take the load instead of the shoulders.
coachingCues: Bar sits on the shoulders, not the hands.
safetyNotes: Practise dumping the bar forward from an empty rack before loading it heavily.
Stop the set the moment the elbows start to drop, because the position is what protects the back.

exercises.name: Box Squat
executionSteps: Set a box or bench so that sitting on it puts your thighs roughly parallel to the floor.
Stand with the bar on your upper back, feet slightly wider than for a normal squat.
Sit back toward the box, keeping your shins close to vertical.
Touch the box under control without relaxing, then stand up by driving through your whole foot.
commonMistakes: Dropping onto the box rather than sitting under control.
Fully relaxing on the box and losing the braced trunk position.
Rocking backward and then swinging forward to start the stand.
coachingCues: Stand up with the chest and hips together.
safetyNotes: Use a squat rack with safety pins set just below your bottom position.
Choose a stable box that will not slide or tip when you touch it.

exercises.name: Leg Press
executionSteps: Sit in the machine with your back and hips flat against the pad.
Place your feet about shoulder width apart in the middle of the platform.
Release the safety catches and lower the platform until your knees reach about ninety degrees.
Press back up without locking the knees out sharply, and reset the catches before you get out.
commonMistakes: Lowering so far that the hips curl up off the pad and round the lower back.
Snapping the knees straight at the top of each repetition.
Pushing on the knees with the hands to force out extra reps.
coachingCues: Hips stay glued to the pad.
Stop just short of locked knees.
safetyNotes: Always engage the safety catches before getting into or out of the machine.
Reduce the range of motion if your hips lift off the pad at the bottom.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
executionSteps: Stand with your back flat against a wall and walk your feet out about two foot lengths.
Slide down the wall until your knees are bent to roughly ninety degrees.
Keep your whole back in contact with the wall and your weight through your heels and midfoot.
Hold for the planned time, then push through your feet to slide back up.
commonMistakes: Setting the feet too close to the wall so the knees travel far past the toes.
Resting the hands on the thighs to take load off the legs.
Holding your breath for the whole set.
safetyNotes: Come out of the hold early if the knees start to ache rather than the thighs burning.
Use a wall that is smooth and dry so you do not slip partway through the hold.

exercises.name: Hip Hinge Drill
executionSteps: Hold a broomstick or light bar along your back so it touches your head, upper back and tailbone.
Stand with feet hip width apart and soften the knees slightly.
Push your hips back and lower your chest, keeping all three contact points on the stick.
Return to standing by driving the hips forward.
commonMistakes: Losing contact between the stick and the lower back, which shows the spine is rounding.
Bending the knees so much that the drill becomes a squat.
Looking straight ahead and craning the neck as the torso comes down.
coachingCues: Three points stay on the stick.
safetyNotes: Move slowly and use this to learn the shape before adding any load.
Reduce the range if you feel pulling in the lower back rather than the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
executionSteps: Stand holding a barbell at the top of a deadlift with your hands just outside your hips.
Soften your knees and hold that knee angle throughout.
Push your hips back and lower the bar down your thighs, keeping it in contact with your legs.
Stop at the end of your hamstring range, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift forward away from the legs.
Rounding the upper back to reach the floor.
Hyperextending the lower back at the top instead of finishing with the glutes.
coachingCues: Shave the legs with the bar.
Squeeze the glutes to finish, do not lean back.
safetyNotes: The bar does not need to reach the floor; range is set by your hamstrings, not the plates.
Use a rack to unload the bar between sets rather than lowering it from standing.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
executionSteps: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Soften your knees and keep them at that angle for the whole repetition.
Push your hips back and let the dumbbells travel down close to your legs.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch behind the thighs, then drive the hips forward to stand up.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees more as you descend, which turns it into a squat.
Letting the dumbbells drift away from the legs and loading the lower back.
Chasing depth by rounding the back instead of stopping at the end of your hamstring range.
coachingCues: Drag the dumbbells down your legs.
Push the hips toward the wall behind you.
Long spine from head to hips.
safetyNotes: Stop the descent as soon as your lower back starts to round.
Set the dumbbells down between sets rather than holding them while you rest.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
executionSteps: Stand with the kettlebell about a foot in front of you and hinge to grip the handle with both hands.
Tilt the bell toward you and hike it back between your legs, above knee height.
Snap your hips forward so the bell swings up to roughly chest height on its own momentum.
Let the bell fall back down and absorb it by hinging again, keeping the arms relaxed.
commonMistakes: Lifting the bell with the arms and shoulders instead of the hips.
Squatting the bell up and down rather than hinging.
Letting the bell swing below the knees and pulling the back into a rounded position.
coachingCues: Snap the hips, do not lift the arms.
Hike it back like a pass between your legs.
safetyNotes: Swing in a clear space with nothing in front of you or behind you.
Stop the set if the bell starts pulling you forward onto your toes.

exercises.name: Cable Pull Through
executionSteps: Set a rope handle at the lowest pulley position and face away from the machine.
Pass the rope between your legs and step forward until the cable is under tension.
Push your hips back with a soft bend in the knees, letting the rope travel between your legs.
Stand tall by squeezing your glutes, without leaning back at the top.
commonMistakes: Turning the movement into a squat by bending the knees instead of the hips.
Pulling with the arms rather than letting the hips do the work.
Leaning backward at the top and stressing the lower back.
coachingCues: Finish standing tall, not leaning back.
safetyNotes: Check that the rope is fully attached before you load the stack.
Keep the weight light enough that the cable cannot pull you off balance.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
executionSteps: Step into the middle of the trap bar with your feet about hip width apart.
Hinge down and take both handles, then set your chest up and take the slack out of the bar.
Push your feet through the floor and stand up, keeping the bar close to your body.
Finish standing tall, then return the bar to the floor by hinging back down under control.
commonMistakes: Yanking the bar off the floor before the slack is taken out.
Letting the hips shoot up first so the legs stop contributing.
Dropping the bar from the top rather than lowering it.
coachingCues: Take the slack out, then push.
safetyNotes: Stop the set if your lower back rounds on the way up rather than adding another repetition.
Keep your feet and shins clear of the frame when you set the bar back down.

exercises.name: Push Up
executionSteps: Set your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder width, under or just below your shoulders.
Straighten your legs and squeeze your glutes so your body forms one line.
Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees.
Press back up to straight arms, keeping the trunk rigid the whole time.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag toward the floor.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Leading with the head and neck instead of the chest.
coachingCues: One straight line, head to heels.
Screw the hands into the floor.
safetyNotes: Raise your hands onto a bench or step if you cannot hold the line at floor level.
Stop if the front of the shoulder pinches, and reduce how far you descend.

exercises.name: Incline Push Up
executionSteps: Place your hands on a bench or a sturdy raised surface, slightly wider than shoulder width.
Walk your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the bench, keeping your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees.
Press back up to straight arms without letting your hips sag or rise.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop so the lower back takes the load.
Dropping the head forward instead of keeping the neck in line with the spine.
Only lowering partway and cutting the range short.
coachingCues: Squeeze the glutes to stop the hips sagging.
safetyNotes: Use a surface that cannot slide or tip under your hands.
Raise the surface to make the movement easier rather than shortening the range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
executionSteps: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh.
Lie back while bringing the dumbbells up to shoulder height, then set your shoulder blades back and down.
Press both dumbbells up until your arms are almost straight, keeping them over your shoulders.
Lower under control until your upper arms are about level with your torso, then press again.
commonMistakes: Lowering the dumbbells so far that the shoulders roll forward.
Letting the dumbbells drift toward the head or the hips instead of tracking over the chest.
Clashing the dumbbells together at the top and losing tension.
coachingCues: Stop the descent when the chest says so.
safetyNotes: Learn to sit up with the dumbbells rather than dropping them beside you.
Choose a weight you can get into position on your own without a spotter.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
executionSteps: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder width and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
Unrack the bar, lower it under control to the lower half of your chest, and pause briefly.
Press the bar back over your shoulders without letting the shoulder blades roll forward.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest to start the press.
Letting the shoulder blades come loose so the shoulders roll forward.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides at ninety degrees.
coachingCues: Shoulder blades pinned to the bench.
Bend the bar apart as you press.
Elbows tucked to about forty-five degrees.
safetyNotes: Use a spotter or a rack with safety arms set just above chest height whenever you train near your limit.
Do not use a thumbless grip; the bar can roll out of the hands.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
executionSteps: Sit on a bench with back support and hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Turn your palms to face forward and set your ribs down so your back is not arched.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are almost straight.
Lower under control back to shoulder height before the next repetition.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to push the weight up.
Pressing the dumbbells forward rather than straight overhead.
Letting the dumbbells drift wide and away from the shoulders.
coachingCues: Press to the ceiling, not the wall.
Finish with the arms beside the ears.
safetyNotes: Reduce the weight if you cannot press without arching the lower back.
Stop the set if you feel pinching at the top of the shoulder rather than working through it.

exercises.name: Cable Chest Press
executionSteps: Set both pulleys at roughly chest height and take a handle in each hand.
Step forward into a split stance so the cables are under tension before you start.
Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight, bringing them slightly together.
Return under control until you feel a stretch across the chest, then press again.
commonMistakes: Standing too close to the machine so there is no tension at the start.
Letting the torso twist to help push one arm through.
Shrugging the shoulders up as the handles come forward.
safetyNotes: Check both handles are clipped in before you step forward into tension.
Return the stack under control rather than letting the plates slam.

exercises.name: Band Row
executionSteps: Anchor a resistance band at about chest height and hold one end in each hand.
Step back until the band is under tension with your arms straight.
Pull your elbows back past your ribs, drawing your shoulder blades together.
Return under control until your arms are straight and your shoulder blades come apart again.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to add range instead of pulling with the arms and back.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears as you pull.
Letting the band snap you forward on the way back.
coachingCues: Control the return, do not release it.
safetyNotes: Check the band and the anchor for wear or nicks before every set.
Never anchor a band at eye level in a way that could snap back toward your face.

exercises.name: One Arm Dumbbell Row
executionSteps: Place one hand and the matching knee on a bench, with the other foot on the floor.
Hold a dumbbell in the free hand and let it hang with the arm straight.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, driving the elbow back past your ribs.
Lower under control until the arm is straight, then repeat before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Twisting the torso to throw the weight up.
Pulling the dumbbell out toward the shoulder instead of back toward the hip.
Rounding the back rather than keeping the torso flat and steady.
coachingCues: Back stays flat like a tabletop.
safetyNotes: Match the repetitions on both sides so one side does not quietly fall behind.
Set the dumbbell down rather than dropping it when the set ends.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
executionSteps: Set the thigh pad so your legs are held down firmly, and take a grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Sit down and let your arms straighten, allowing the shoulders to rise.
Pull your shoulder blades down first, then draw the bar to your upper chest.
Return the bar under control until your arms are straight again.
commonMistakes: Leaning far back and turning the movement into a row.
Pulling the bar behind the neck.
Letting the weight stack pull the arms up quickly at the end of each rep.
safetyNotes: Pull to the front of the body rather than behind the neck.
Set the thigh pad snugly so you are not pulled up off the seat.

exercises.name: Pull Up
executionSteps: Take an overhand grip on the bar, a little wider than shoulder width.
Hang with straight arms and pull your shoulder blades down away from your ears.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, keeping the ribs down and the legs still.
Lower all the way back to straight arms under control.
commonMistakes: Swinging the legs to generate momentum.
Stopping halfway down instead of returning to a full hang.
Craning the chin over the bar while the chest stays low.
safetyNotes: Check the bar is secure and rated for your bodyweight before hanging from it.
Use a band or an assisted machine to build up rather than kipping to reach a rep count.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
executionSteps: Sit facing the machine with your feet on the platform and a slight bend in your knees.
Take the handle and sit tall with your arms straight and the cable under tension.
Pull the handle to your stomach, driving your elbows back past your ribs.
Return under control, letting your shoulder blades come apart without letting your back round.
commonMistakes: Rocking the torso back and forth to move the weight.
Rounding the lower back as the handle returns.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears at the end of the pull.
coachingCues: Let the blades travel, not the spine.
safetyNotes: Keep a soft bend in the knees so the load does not park on the lower back.
Let the stack down under control rather than releasing the handle at the end of the set.

exercises.name: Face Pull
executionSteps: Attach a rope to a pulley set at roughly head height.
Take one end in each hand with your thumbs pointing back, and step away until the cable is tight.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating your hands and driving your elbows high and wide.
Pause briefly with the hands beside your head, then return under control.
commonMistakes: Using so much weight that the whole body rocks backward.
Letting the elbows drop so the movement becomes a row.
Shrugging the shoulders up instead of pulling the shoulder blades back.
coachingCues: Pull the rope apart, not just back.
safetyNotes: Keep the load light; this is a positioning exercise rather than a strength test.
Stop if the front of the shoulder pinches and lower the pulley height slightly.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
executionSteps: Set a dumbbell on each side of you and hinge down to grip both handles.
Stand up with a flat back and let the weights hang at your sides.
Set your shoulders down and back, brace your stomach, and walk with short controlled steps.
Walk the planned distance or time, then hinge down to set the weights back on the floor.
commonMistakes: Letting the shoulders round forward under the load.
Leaning back to counterbalance the weight.
Dropping the weights from standing at the end of the carry.
safetyNotes: Walk a clear route with no obstacles or trip hazards.
Set the weights down under control rather than dropping them near your feet.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
executionSteps: Set a kettlebell beside one foot and hinge down to take the handle.
Stand up with a flat back and let the bell hang at your side.
Resist the pull to that side so your shoulders and hips stay level.
Walk the planned distance, set the bell down, then repeat carrying on the other side.
commonMistakes: Leaning away from the weight instead of staying upright.
Letting the loaded shoulder drop toward the floor.
Carrying only on one side and never matching it on the other.
coachingCues: Stand as if you were carrying nothing.
Match the distance on both sides.
safetyNotes: Always carry the same distance on each side so the trunk is trained evenly.
Set the bell down by hinging rather than bending sideways at the waist.

exercises.name: Front Rack Carry
executionSteps: Clean or lift two kettlebells to the front rack position, resting on the forearms against the chest.
Keep the elbows down and in, and the wrists straight.
Brace your stomach and breathe shallowly, then walk with controlled steps.
Complete the planned distance, then lower the bells to your shoulders and down to the floor.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare out, which drags the chest down.
Arching the lower back to counter the front load.
Holding the breath for the whole carry.
safetyNotes: Learn the rack position with one light bell before carrying two.
Stop the carry when the position breaks down rather than when the distance ends.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry
executionSteps: Press a dumbbell overhead in each hand until the arms are straight.
Lock the elbows, set the shoulder blades, and bring the arms close to the ears.
Brace hard and walk with slow deliberate steps, keeping the weights still.
Complete the distance, then lower the weights to the shoulders and down under control.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back to hold the weights up.
Letting the arms drift forward in front of the head.
Walking quickly so the weights start to wobble.
safetyNotes: Start very light; overhead carrying exposes shoulder and trunk positioning quickly.
Stop and lower the weights safely the moment the arms start to drift forward.

exercises.name: Sandbag Bear Hug Carry
executionSteps: Squat down to the sandbag and wrap both arms around it.
Pull it tight against your chest and stand up with a flat back.
Brace your stomach and keep your chest up against the bag pulling you forward.
Walk the planned distance, then squat down to set the bag back on the floor.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back to lift the bag off the floor.
Letting the bag slide down so the arms take all the work.
Dropping the bag from standing height at the end of the carry.
coachingCues: Hug it high on the chest.
Squat it down, do not drop it.
safetyNotes: Practise picking the bag up with a light load before carrying a heavy one.
Keep your feet clear when you set the bag down.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch Carry
executionSteps: Stand two weight plates together with the smooth sides facing out.
Pinch them between your thumb and fingers and stand up with a flat back.
Let the plates hang at your side and keep your shoulder set down and back.
Walk the planned distance, then lower the plates under control before your grip fails.
commonMistakes: Resting the plates against the thigh to reduce the grip demand.
Carrying on until the plates slip out of the hand.
Leaning away from the load rather than staying tall.
coachingCues: Pinch hard from the first step.
Plates hang free of the leg.
safetyNotes: Carry over a floor you do not mind dropping a plate on, and keep your feet clear.
End the set while you still control the plates rather than when they fall.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
executionSteps: Set a cable at chest height and stand side on with your feet about shoulder width apart.
Hold the handle in both hands at your sternum and step away until the cable is under tension.
Press the handle straight out in front of you and resist the pull toward the machine.
Return the handle to your chest under control, and complete the set before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Letting the torso turn toward the machine as the arms extend.
Pressing high or low rather than straight out from the sternum.
Loading it so heavily that the trunk cannot stay square.
coachingCues: Press straight out from the chest.
safetyNotes: Choose a load you can hold without rotating; this is an anti-rotation exercise.
Keep the feet planted rather than pivoting to make the press easier.

exercises.name: Band Anti Rotation Hold
executionSteps: Anchor a band at chest height and stand side on to the anchor.
Hold the band in both hands and press it straight out in front of your sternum.
Step away until the band is trying to rotate you toward the anchor.
Hold still for the planned time, then switch sides so both directions are trained.
commonMistakes: Letting the arms drift toward the anchor as the trunk gives in.
Bracing by holding the breath instead of breathing through the hold.
Standing so close that the band provides almost no resistance.
coachingCues: Hands stay in the centre of the chest.
safetyNotes: Inspect the band and anchor point before each set.
Step out gradually rather than jumping into full tension.

exercises.name: Cable Wood Chop
executionSteps: Set the pulley high and stand side on with your feet a little wider than the hips.
Take the handle in both hands with your arms fairly straight.
Pull down and across your body toward the opposite hip, turning through the trunk and hips together.
Return under control along the same path, then complete the set before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Turning only at the arms and shoulders while the hips stay locked.
Twisting the lower back rather than rotating through the whole trunk.
Using so much load that the return is uncontrolled.
coachingCues: Turn the chest and hips together.
safetyNotes: Keep the load moderate; rotation under heavy load is hard to control.
Stop if you feel a twinge in the lower back rather than working through it.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
executionSteps: Stand side on to a solid wall, about an arm and a ball length away.
Hold the ball at chest height with your weight slightly on the back foot.
Turn the back hip through and throw the ball into the wall, letting the trunk follow the hips.
Catch or collect the ball, reset your stance, and repeat before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Throwing with the arms alone while the hips stay still.
Standing too close, so there is no room to turn.
Using a bouncy ball that rebounds unpredictably.
coachingCues: Fast and light, not heavy and slow.
safetyNotes: Use a wall that can take repeated impact, and check nobody is standing in the rebound path.
Warm up before throwing; this is a fast movement and cold tissue tolerates it poorly.

exercises.name: Half Kneeling Cable Lift
executionSteps: Set the pulley low and kneel side on with the inside knee down.
Take the handle in both hands near the down knee, with your arms fairly straight.
Pull up and across your body toward the opposite shoulder, rotating through the trunk.
Return under control, and complete the set before switching sides.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sink to one side instead of staying tall in the kneeling position.
Pulling with the arms while the trunk stays still.
Leaning back at the top of the lift.
coachingCues: Turn the chest, then the arms follow.
Ribs stay down at the top.
safetyNotes: Kneel on a pad to protect the down knee.
Keep the load light enough that the cable cannot pull you off balance.

exercises.name: Dead Bug With Reach
executionSteps: Lie on your back with your arms straight above your shoulders and your knees over your hips.
Press your lower back gently into the floor and keep it there.
Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start under control and repeat on the other side.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch as the limbs reach away.
Moving quickly so the trunk never really has to work.
Holding the breath rather than exhaling as the limbs extend.
coachingCues: Move slowly, opposite arm and leg.
safetyNotes: Shorten the reach if your back lifts off the floor.
This should feel like work in the stomach, not the lower back.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
executionSteps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart.
Step one foot straight back and land on the ball of that foot.
Lower until the back knee is just above the floor and the front thigh is roughly parallel.
Push through the front foot to bring the back leg forward and return to standing.
commonMistakes: Stepping back on a diagonal, which narrows the base and unsettles balance.
Letting the torso fall forward over the front thigh.
Pushing off the back toes to stand instead of loading the front leg.
safetyNotes: Place a folded mat under the back knee while you are learning the depth.
Hold a support for balance rather than shortening the range.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
executionSteps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms by your sides.
Step forward far enough that both knees can bend to about ninety degrees.
Lower until the back knee is just above the floor, keeping the torso upright.
Drive through the front foot to stand, bring the back foot through, and step into the next lunge.
commonMistakes: Taking a short step so the front knee travels a long way forward.
Leaning the torso over the front thigh.
Letting the back knee bang into the floor.
coachingCues: Kiss the floor with the back knee.
Push the floor away to stand.
safetyNotes: Walk in a clear straight lane with room to finish the set.
Reduce the load or switch to a static lunge if your balance is wavering.

exercises.name: Split Squat
executionSteps: Step one foot forward into a split stance about one stride long.
Keep the front foot flat and rise onto the ball of the back foot.
Lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor.
Drive up through the front foot without moving your feet, and finish the set before swapping.
commonMistakes: Setting the stance too short, so the front knee is crowded at the bottom.
Drifting forward and back instead of moving straight up and down.
Letting the hips rotate so the two sides are no longer square.
coachingCues: Move like a lift, straight up and down.
Hips stay square to the front.
safetyNotes: Use a wall or rack for balance until the position feels stable.
Reduce the depth if the front of the back hip feels pinched.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
executionSteps: Stand about a stride in front of a bench and rest the top of your back foot on it.
Check the front foot is far enough forward that the knee stays over the midfoot at the bottom.
Lower straight down until the back knee is close to the floor.
Drive up through the front foot, then finish all the reps before swapping legs.
commonMistakes: Standing too close to the bench, which crowds the front knee.
Pushing off the back foot instead of loading the front leg.
Letting the front knee collapse inward under fatigue.
coachingCues: Back leg is a kickstand, not an engine.
Front knee tracks over the second toe.
safetyNotes: Hold a rack or wall for balance while you learn the position.
Use a lower surface for the back foot if the front of the rear hip feels pinched.

exercises.name: Step Up
executionSteps: Set a box at a height where your thigh is roughly parallel to the floor when your foot is on it.
Place one whole foot on the box, with the heel well inside the edge.
Push through that foot to stand up on the box without pushing off the floor with the other leg.
Lower back down under control on the same leg, then repeat before swapping sides.
commonMistakes: Pushing off the trailing foot to help the working leg.
Placing only part of the foot on the box so the heel hangs over the edge.
Dropping back to the floor rather than lowering under control.
safetyNotes: Use a box that cannot slide or tip, and check it before every set.
Lower the box height if you cannot control the way down.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
executionSteps: Stand tall with your feet together and your toes pointing forward.
Take a wide step directly out to one side, keeping both feet flat and facing forward.
Push your hips back and bend the stepping knee while the other leg stays straight.
Push off the bent leg to return to standing, then repeat before changing sides.
commonMistakes: Turning the stepping foot outward so the movement becomes a lunge on an angle.
Letting the inside edge of the foot lift as you sit into the side.
Bending the trailing knee instead of keeping that leg long.
coachingCues: Hips back, not just knee out.
safetyNotes: Ease into the range gradually; the inner thigh is easy to strain when cold.
Reduce the width of the step if you feel a pull rather than a stretch on the inside of the leg.

exercises.name: Forearm Plank
executionSteps: Set your forearms on the floor with your elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you and rise onto your toes.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your stomach so your body forms a straight line.
Hold for the planned time, breathing steadily, then lower your knees to finish.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag so the lower back takes the load.
Lifting the hips high into an inverted V to make the hold easier.
Holding the breath for the duration of the set.
coachingCues: Pull the elbows toward the toes without moving them.
safetyNotes: End the hold as soon as the hips start to drop rather than pushing for time.
Drop to your knees if you feel it in your lower back instead of your stomach.

exercises.name: Side Plank
executionSteps: Lie on one side with your elbow under your shoulder and your legs stacked.
Press your forearm into the floor and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Keep your head in line with your spine and your top hip stacked over the bottom one.
Hold for the planned time, then lower under control and repeat on the other side.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sink toward the floor during the hold.
Rotating the top hip forward so the position becomes a partial front plank.
Placing the elbow ahead of or behind the shoulder.
coachingCues: Push the floor away and lift the ribs.
safetyNotes: Bend the bottom knee and rest it on the floor to reduce the load while you build up.
Match the hold time on both sides so one side does not lag behind.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
executionSteps: Lie on your back and press your lower back flat into the floor.
Lift your shoulder blades off the floor and reach your arms past your ears.
Raise your legs and lower them until just before your back lifts away from the floor.
Hold that position, breathing shallowly, then lower everything to finish.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch away from the floor as the legs come down.
Pulling on the head with the hands to hold the shoulders up.
Holding the breath rather than breathing into the position.
coachingCues: Lower back glued to the floor.
Raise the legs if the back lifts.
safetyNotes: Bend the knees or keep the legs higher to make the hold manageable.
Stop the moment the lower back arches, because that is where the position stops working.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Stir The Pot
executionSteps: Set your forearms on a stability ball and extend your legs behind you into a plank.
Squeeze your glutes and brace hard, since the ball will move at any loss of tension.
Draw small circles with your forearms while keeping your hips and spine completely still.
Complete the planned circles in each direction, then lower your knees to finish.
commonMistakes: Drawing circles so large that the hips start to sway.
Letting the hips drop as the trunk fatigues.
Rushing the circles instead of moving slowly and staying rigid.
coachingCues: The arms move, nothing else does.
safetyNotes: Position the ball against a wall while you are learning so it cannot roll away.
End the set as soon as the hips start to move rather than pushing for more circles.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
executionSteps: Attach a rope to a high pulley and kneel facing the machine.
Hold the rope beside your head and hinge slightly forward to load the cable.
Curl your ribs toward your hips, rounding the upper back rather than folding at the hips.
Return under control until you feel your abdominals lengthen, without letting the weight pull you up.
commonMistakes: Bending at the hips so the movement becomes a hinge rather than a trunk curl.
Pulling with the arms and shoulders instead of the abdominals.
Letting the stack yank the torso back up between reps.
coachingCues: Hands stay glued to the head.
safetyNotes: Kneel on a pad and check the rope attachment before adding load.
Stop if you feel strain in the neck rather than work in the abdominals.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
executionSteps: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and your arms straight.
Pull your shoulder blades down so you are not hanging loose from the shoulders.
Raise both knees toward your chest by curling the pelvis, not just bending the hips.
Lower under control until your legs hang straight again, without swinging.
commonMistakes: Swinging the legs and using momentum from a previous repetition.
Only bending at the hips so the abdominals barely work.
Dropping the legs quickly and starting the next rep from the swing.
safetyNotes: Check the bar is secure before hanging from it.
Use straps or a padded bar if your grip gives out before your abdominals do.

exercises.name: Brisk Walk
executionSteps: Start at an easy pace for two to three minutes to let your breathing settle.
Pick up the pace until talking becomes slightly effortful but still possible.
Keep your posture tall with a relaxed arm swing and a steady rhythm.
Finish with two to three minutes of easy walking to bring the heart rate down.
commonMistakes: Starting at the target pace with no warm-up.
Overstriding, which lands the heel far in front and jars the knee.
Hunching forward over a phone and losing the tall posture.
safetyNotes: Choose even ground and footwear with grip if conditions are wet.
Slow down if you become dizzy, unusually breathless, or feel chest discomfort.

exercises.name: Treadmill Run
executionSteps: Attach the safety key before you start the belt.
Begin with several minutes of walking, then raise the speed gradually.
Run near the front of the belt with a tall posture and a relaxed arm swing.
Lower the speed gradually at the end rather than stepping straight off.
commonMistakes: Holding the handrails while running, which changes the stride and posture.
Drifting toward the back of the belt.
Jumping onto a belt that is already moving quickly.
coachingCues: Stay near the front of the belt.
safetyNotes: Always clip the safety key to your clothing so the belt stops if you fall.
Stop immediately if you feel chest discomfort, dizziness, or unusual breathlessness.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
executionSteps: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent when the pedal is at its lowest point.
Start pedalling at an easy resistance for a few minutes to warm up.
Raise the resistance or cadence until your breathing matches the intended effort.
Finish with a few minutes of easy pedalling before you get off.
commonMistakes: Riding with the saddle too low, which cramps the knees.
Rocking the hips side to side because the saddle is too high.
Gripping the handlebars hard and hunching the shoulders.
coachingCues: Hips stay still in the saddle.
safetyNotes: Check the saddle and handlebar clamps are tight before you start.
Stop and rest if you feel dizzy, light-headed, or any chest discomfort.

exercises.name: Row Ergometer
executionSteps: Strap your feet in and sit with your shins vertical and your arms straight.
Drive with the legs first, keeping the arms long and the back braced.
As the legs finish, swing the torso back slightly and then pull the handle to the lower ribs.
Reverse the order on the recovery: arms away, then torso, then let the knees bend.
commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms before the legs have finished driving.
Rounding the back at the front of the stroke.
Rushing the recovery so the next stroke starts from a poor position.
coachingCues: Legs, body, arms. Then arms, body, legs.
safetyNotes: Set the foot straps over the widest part of the foot so your heels stay in contact.
Reduce the damper setting if your lower back tires before your legs do.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
executionSteps: Set the rope length so the handles reach about armpit height when you stand on the middle.
Hold the handles near your hips with your elbows close to your sides.
Turn the rope with your wrists and hop just high enough to clear it.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and keep the rhythm steady.
commonMistakes: Jumping far higher than the rope requires.
Turning the rope with the whole arm instead of the wrists.
Landing flat and heavy on stiff legs.
safetyNotes: Jump on a forgiving surface rather than concrete where possible.
Build up the duration gradually, because the calves and Achilles take time to adapt.

exercises.name: Low Impact Step March
executionSteps: Stand tall with your feet hip width apart and your arms relaxed.
Lift one knee to about hip height while swinging the opposite arm.
Place the foot down softly and repeat on the other side.
Build to a steady rhythm you can hold for the planned time.
commonMistakes: Leaning back as the knee comes up.
Slapping the foot down instead of placing it.
Losing the rhythm and drifting to a stop halfway through.
coachingCues: Tall posture, knee to hip height.
safetyNotes: Hold a chair or wall for balance if you need it; this stays effective either way.
Lower the knee height rather than stopping if the hip flexors start to fatigue.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
executionSteps: Step one foot forward into a long lunge and place both hands on the floor inside the front foot.
Drop the back knee if you need to, and let the front hip sink toward the floor.
Rotate your torso and reach the inside arm toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Return the hand to the floor and repeat, then switch legs.
commonMistakes: Taking a short lunge, which leaves no room for the hip to open.
Rotating from the lower back instead of the upper back.
Rushing through so nothing has time to lengthen.
coachingCues: Turn from the ribs, not the waist.
Follow the hand with your eyes.
safetyNotes: Keep the back knee on the floor while you are learning the position.
Ease back if the front hip pinches rather than stretches.

exercises.name: Cat Cow
executionSteps: Start on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Exhale and round your spine, tucking your tailbone and letting your head drop.
Inhale and reverse it, lifting your tailbone and chest while letting your stomach drop.
Move slowly between the two positions for the planned repetitions.
commonMistakes: Moving quickly so only the middle of the back actually moves.
Pushing into an extreme range at each end rather than moving through the middle.
Letting the elbows bend and the shoulders creep toward the ears.
coachingCues: Move one vertebra at a time.
safetyNotes: Use a mat or padding under the knees.
Reduce the range at either end if you feel pinching rather than easy movement.

exercises.name: Half Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
executionSteps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you.
Tuck your tailbone under so your lower back flattens slightly.
Squeeze the glute on the kneeling side and shift your weight gently forward.
Hold for the planned time while breathing steadily, then swap sides.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back and calling it a hip stretch.
Pushing forward so far that the front knee travels well past the toes.
Skipping the glute squeeze, which is what makes the stretch reach the hip.
safetyNotes: Use a pad under the kneeling knee.
Ease off if you feel pinching at the front of the front hip.

exercises.name: Thoracic Open Book
executionSteps: Lie on your side with your knees bent to about ninety degrees and stacked.
Stretch both arms out in front of you at shoulder height, palms together.
Keeping the knees down, open the top arm across your body and follow it with your eyes.
Return slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions, then swap sides.
commonMistakes: Letting the knees roll open, which turns it into a lower back twist.
Rushing the movement rather than letting the upper back open gradually.
Holding the breath through the rotation.
coachingCues: Lead with the eyes, then the arm.
safetyNotes: Rest the knees on a cushion if holding them down is uncomfortable.
Movement should be felt in the upper back, not the lower back.

exercises.name: Banded Ankle Mobilization
executionSteps: Loop a band around a low anchor and around the front of your ankle, just below the joint line.
Step away so the band pulls your ankle back toward the anchor.
Put that foot on a low step and drive your knee forward over your toes, keeping the heel down.
Rock in and out of the position for the planned repetitions, then swap sides.
commonMistakes: Letting the heel lift as the knee travels forward.
Placing the band across the foot rather than just below the ankle joint.
Forcing the range instead of easing into it.
coachingCues: Knee travels over the second toe.
safetyNotes: Check the band for damage and make sure the anchor is secure.
This should feel like a stretch at the front of the ankle, not pinching or pain.

exercises.name: Shoulder Wall Slide
executionSteps: Stand with your back against a wall and your feet a short step away from it.
Place your forearms on the wall with your elbows at about shoulder height.
Keep your lower back gently pressed toward the wall and slide your arms upward.
Slide back down under control, stopping wherever contact with the wall is lost.
commonMistakes: Arching the lower back away from the wall to gain more range.
Letting the forearms come off the wall as the arms rise.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
coachingCues: Ribs down, back near the wall.
safetyNotes: Range is limited by what you can do without arching; do not chase a higher reach.
Stop if the shoulder pinches at the top of the slide.
